exocrine signals

insulin → muscle and fat take up glucose (GLUT4); liver stores glycogen and releases less glucose

glucagon → liver releases glucose (glycogen breakdown, gluconeogenesis)

in the duodenum → enteropeptidase cuts trypsinogen to trypsin, which activates the other proenzymes; amylase and lipase are secreted already active (Fieker et al. 2011, PMID 21753892)

glucose ATP Ca²⁺ insulin glucagon somatostatin enzymes HCO₃⁻ juice blood

Hover or focus a part for an explanation. Drag glucose low: the K-ATP gate reopens, insulin stops and glucagon release rises. Drag it high: insulin and somatostatin release rise.

Sources and notes

Educational only, not medical advice. Schematic, not to scale; one acinus and one islet stand for the gland. Blood glucose is set by the slider; this figure has no feedback loop, so insulin and glucagon do not change it. Levels come from a qualitative model, not measurements, and no number is shown. Unlabelled parts (channels, transporter, mitochondrion, granules) are named on hover. On a phone, scroll the figure sideways.

  • Exocrine pancreas. Acinar synthesis on the rough ER, zymogen granules at the apical pole, Ca²⁺-dependent secretion to acetylcholine and CCK, activation of trypsinogen by enteropeptidase in the duodenum: Pandol SJ, The Exocrine Pancreas, Morgan & Claypool 2010 (NCBI Bookshelf NBK54128). CCK on human acinar cells is contested, so the evidence is mixed: no response in Ji et al., Gastroenterology 2001, a direct Ca²⁺ and secretory response in Murphy et al., Gastroenterology 2008. Lipases and amylase are secreted active, proteases as proenzymes: Fieker et al., Clin Exp Gastroenterol 2011.
  • Duct fluid. Secretin → cAMP/PKA → CFTR with the SLC26A6 Cl⁻/HCO₃⁻ exchanger, giving HCO₃⁻-rich fluid from duct cells; Gq–PLC–IP₃ Ca²⁺ signalling in secretory cells; Ca²⁺–cAMP synergy: Lee et al., Physiol Rev 2012.
  • Beta-cell stimulus–secretion coupling. Glucose metabolism, ATP/ADP, K-ATP closure, depolarisation, voltage-gated Ca²⁺ entry and exocytosis, with mouse–human differences: Rorsman and Ashcroft, Physiol Rev 2018. Glucokinase as the glucose sensor; ATP and MgADP on K-ATP. Glucose transporter: GLUT2 in rodent beta cells, GLUT1 in human (De Vos et al., J Clin Invest 1995).
  • Islet cells and glucose homeostasis. Insulin, glucagon and somatostatin actions; liver, muscle and fat as targets: Röder et al., Exp Mol Med 2016. Human islets intermix the cell types rather than forming a beta-cell core: Cabrera et al., PNAS 2006. Somatostatin secretion rises with glucose; somatostatin receptors couple to an inhibitory G protein: Rorsman and Huising, Nat Rev Endocrinol 2018. Fenestrated islet capillaries: Zanone et al., Curr Diabetes Rev 2008.

Simplified. Cell sizes, counts, positions and speeds are illustrative and time is compressed. CCK/ACh and secretin are shown as independent switches, but in the body they potentiate each other (Ca²⁺–cAMP synergy, Lee et al. 2012). Not drawn: the Golgi, centroacinar cells, amplifying (K-ATP-independent) pathways, incretins, the GLUT4 step in muscle and fat, the feedback of insulin and glucagon on blood glucose, and the islet's real cell proportions. The Ji 2001 and Murphy 2008 results on CCK differ and are not reconciled here.
